{
  "research_question": "Do stimulation paradigms (Combined, ICMS Only, Dim Visual Only, Bright Visual Only, Sham) differentially affect mouse navigation performance as measured by Time-to-Target, Success, Path Efficiency, Average Speed, and Angular Dispersion (AD)?",
  "stim_paradigms_compared": ["Combined", "ICMS Only", "Dim Visual Only", "Bright Visual Only", "Sham"],
  "response_variables": ["Time-to-Target", "Success", "Path Efficiency", "Average Speed", "AD"],
  "anova_plan": [
    "For Time-to-Target: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm as fixed factor. Log-transform consideration due to right skew (max=201.39 vs mean=2.81).",
    "For Success: One-way ANOVA inappropriate due to binary nature (0/1). Use binary logistic regression or chi-square test of independence with Stim Paradigm. If ANOVA insisted upon, arcsine-sqrt transformation of proportions per group, but this loses individual-level information.",
    "For Path Efficiency: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Consider log transformation due to extreme maximum (29.82 vs mean=0.47) indicating heavy right tail.",
    "For Average Speed: One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Check for outliers (max=75.35 vs mean=12.50) and consider robust ANOVA or transformation.",
    "For AD (Angular Dispersion): One-way ANOVA with Stim Paradigm. Bounded [0,1] variable; consider beta regression or arcsine-square-root transformation if variance near boundaries differs."
  ],
  "assumptions_and_diagnostics": [
    "Independence: Violation likely due to repeated measures within 8 mice; use mixed-effects models or account for Mouse as random effect.",
    "Normality: Q-Q plots and Shapiro-Wilk tests per group; severe skew expected for Time-to-Target and Path Efficiency based on max/mean ratios.",
    "Homoscedasticity: Levene's test; unequal group sizes (n=3323 to 48846) reduce robustness, though large N provides some protection.",
    "Outliers: Boxplots for each response by paradigm; extreme max values in Time-to-Target (201.39), Path Efficiency (29.82), and Average Speed (75.35) suggest data cleaning or winsorization may be needed.",
    "For Success (binary): No ANOVA assumptions apply; logistic regression assumptions (linearity in logit, no overdispersion) must be checked."
  ],
  "posthoc_plan": [
    "If omnibus ANOVA significant: Tukey HSD for pairwise comparisons controlling familywise error, though unequal sample sizes require Tukey-Kramer adjustment.",
    "For Success (logistic regression): Pairwise odds ratios with Bonferroni or Holm correction for 10 comparisons.",
    "Planned contrasts: Combined vs all others (optimal performance expected), Sham vs all stimulation conditions (baseline impairment), ICMS Only vs Visual Only conditions (modality comparison).",
    "Effect sizes: Partial eta-squared for ANOVA, Cohen's d for pairwise comparisons, odds ratios for Success."
  ],
  "expected_findings": [
    "Sham expected to show poorest performance: lowest Success (0.273), highest Time-to-Target (4.68), lowest Path Efficiency (0.308), lowest Average Speed (10.74), lowest AD (0.236).",
    "Combined expected to show best or near-best performance: high Success (0.780), low Time-to-Target (2.56), high Path Efficiency (0.502), high Average Speed (12.83), high AD (0.399).",
    "Bright Visual Only vs Dim Visual Only: Bright may outperform Dim on Success (0.785 vs 0.673) and Time-to-Target (2.61 vs 3.14), with higher AD (0.387 vs 0.336).",
    "ICMS Only intermediate between Combined and Dim Visual Only on most metrics.",
    "Large sample sizes will yield statistically significant differences even for small effect sizes; practical significance must be evaluated via effect sizes."
  ],
  "limitations": [
    "Severe imbalance in group sizes: Combined (n=48846) dominates Sham (n=3505) by 14:1 ratio, reducing power for Sham comparisons and affecting variance homogeneity.",
    "Repeated measures structure ignored by simple ANOVA: 8 mice contribute multiple trials, violating independence assumption; within-mouse correlation likely substantial.",
    "Success is binary: ANOVA inappropriate; logistic regression or generalized linear mixed model required.",
    "AD bounded [0,1]: Standard ANOVA may predict impossible values; beta regression more appropriate.",
    "Extreme outliers present in all continuous variables, potentially distorting mean differences.",
    "No information on trial sequence, learning effects, or session structure; temporal confounds possible.",
    "No covariates (e.g., difficulty, target distance) available for adjustment."
  ],
  "recommended_next_analysis": "Fit linear mixed-effects models (LMMs) for continuous outcomes and generalized linear mixed-effects models (GLMMs, binomial family) for Success, with Mouse as random intercept and Stim Paradigm as fixed effect. Use likelihood ratio tests for omnibus effects and Satterthwaite or Kenward-Roger approximations for degrees of freedom. For bounded AD, implement beta mixed-effects regression. Apply Bonferroni-Holm correction for 10 pairwise comparisons. Examine residuals and consider robust mixed models if outliers persist."
}
